textbookText: 1. Which of the following is not a fundamental particle? A. electron B. proton C. neutrino D. quark
2. Which combination of up (u) and down (d) quarks forms a proton? A. u u u B. u u d C. u d d D. d d d
3. Baryons and mesons are types of particles that consist of quarks. Which row of the table below shows a possible quark composition for a baryon, and for a meson?
4. The group of particles known as hadrons is composed of quarks. There are two sub-
groups of hadrons: mesons and baryons.
a) What is the name of the property that defines a hadron?
b) State the quark structure of a meson.
c) State the quark structure of a baryon.
d) The antiproton is the antiparticle of the proton. State one way that the proton and
the antiproton are similar, and one way that they are different.
